html:
The largest slave revolt in Roman history, from 73 to 71 BCE, led by the gladiator Spartacus. Romans called it the Third Servile War, after two earlier revolts in Sicily such as the First Servile War.

It began when about seventy gladiators broke out of a training school at Capua. They camped on Mount Vesuvius, and when a Roman force blocked the way down they climbed down the cliffs on ropes of vines and took it by surprise. Runaway slaves joined in their tens of thousands. Led by Spartacus, Crixus and Oenomaus, they beat a string of Roman armies, including both consuls in 72 BCE, and roamed the length of Italy.

The Senate gave the command to Marcus Crassus, one of the richest men in Rome. He restored discipline, reportedly by killing one in ten of a unit that ran, and penned the rebels in the toe of Italy behind a long ditch. In 71 BCE they broke out and were destroyed in Lucania. Six thousand captives were crucified along the Appian Way from Capua to Rome. Pompey, back from Spain, caught some fugitives and claimed a share of the credit, which Crassus resented.
sum: The largest slave revolt in Roman history, from 73 to 71 BCE, led by the gladiator Spartacus. Romans called it the Third Servile War, after two earlier revolts in Sicily such as the First Servile War.
